explanation: A pointer value can designate an object in memory. The address operator & obtains an address, and the indirection operator * accesses the object designated by a valid pointer.
exampleExplanation: address contains the address of score. Dereferencing address lets the last line update score.
misconceptions: The star in a pointer declaration describes a type. The star in an expression dereferences a value.
A variable of pointer type can still hold a null, uninitialized, or dangling value. The type alone does not prove dereferencing it is safe.

reference.title: Local C reference on address and indirection
reference.text: For an object x of type T, &x has type pointer to T. Applying unary * to a valid pointer to T produces an expression designating the referenced object. Check both the pointer type and whether the referenced object exists at the time of access.
